before:
The Cartesian product $A\times B\times C$ consists of all ordered triples whose first coordinate belongs to $A,$ second coordinate belongs to $B,$ and the third coordinate belongs to $C.$

In this case, $A\times A\times B$ consists of every combination of ${a,b}$ with ${a,b}$ and ${1,2},$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}A\times A\times B={ & (a,a,1),(a,a,2),(a,b,1),(a,b,2), \\  & (b,a,1),(b,a,2),(b,b,1),(b,b,2)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that

$$
|A\times A\times B|=|A|\cdot |A|\cdot |B|=2\cdot 2\cdot 2=8.
$$

From the given options, we see that both $(a,a,1)$ and $(b,a,2)$ are in $A\times A\times B.$

Therefore, the correct answer is $(a,a,1)$; $(b,a,2)$ only.

before:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

In this case, $A\times B$ consists of every combination of ${4,8}$ with ${x,y,z},$ as shown in the schematic below.

![](images/72/72feee192b949dcce7b0f10f4e1d772c809bcf73de6c66f15c7de75a4a1ff672.png)

Hence, the set $A\times B$ is given by

$$
A\times B={(4,x),(4,y),(4,z),(8,x),(8,y),(8,z)}.
$$

Note that 

$$
|A\times B|=|A|\cdot |B|=2\cdot 3=6.
$$

Now, the Cartesian product

$$
A\times (A\times B)
$$

consists of every combination of $A$ and $A\times B,$ as shown in the schematic below.

![](images/1a/1ae41857d4aee82a2a4ad838c20bbe72b05a1505a5f4df3aa4a86fda0fff0612.png)

Note that 

$$
|A\times (A\times B)|=|A|\cdot |A\times B|=2\cdot 6=12.
$$

From the given options, we see that both $(4,(8,z))$ and $(8,(8,x))$ are in $A\times \text{\(}A\times B).$

Therefore, the correct answer is $(4,(8,z))$; $(8,(8,x))$ only.
